claim: Forgetting in LLM post-training extends beyond parametric knowledge, with particularly strong drift in robustness and default behavioral preferences.
falsifier: For a given LLM and post-training procedure, measure parametric knowledge retention (e.g., factual recall) alongside robustness (e.g., adversarial input stability) and default behavioral preferences (e.g., output style or safety tendencies) before and after training; the claim predicts that robustness and behavioral preferences will show larger relative drift than parametric knowledge.

conditions: Post-training applied to already aligned models
Evaluation using CapTrack framework across multiple model families, domains, and algorithms
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported model families, domains, and post-training algorithms; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Post-training–Forgetting, including drift principle

claim: Integrating multiple biological data layers (sequence, structure, and evolutionary information) improves PTM site prediction accuracy compared to using only single data layers.
falsifier: One could compare PTM prediction performance of a model using only sequence features against a model that also incorporates structural and evolutionary features on a benchmark dataset.

conditions: when predicting PTM sites from protein sequences
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task, population, and conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Multi-modal integration of sequence for prediction accuracy

claim: Increasing substrate temperature during PECVD growth increases the mean free path of plasma species, which is directly proportional to temperature.
falsifier: The relationship can be tested by measuring plasma species mean free path (e.g., via Langmuir probe or optical emission spectroscopy) at different substrate temperatures in a PECVD reactor.

exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported PECVD system and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Increase in substrate temperature–Increase in mean free principle
